topics.label: What do you know of Vorannuhl?
topics.intent: A hunter of Noota Nara (the village's own talker; the place's build names her). Tells: Vorannuhl is the Dunmer town east along the south slope that the old plague emptied; nobody has robbed it because its dead still walk; Sarpa raiders camp in its yard this season and shoot anyone who comes near.

topics.label: Remind me what we are hunting, and why.
topics.intent: Never-Writes-Twice, at the back of Nesh-Deekas House. Tells: the Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings jewel, cut from Hist amber. It sits at the Root, the place under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire where the roots of every Hist meet. Used where it sits, it pours strength down every root and heals every sick tree; lifted from its place, it cuts every tree from every other for good. The last king shut it behind the Kings Gate, which opens only with its three seal-stones: the thiefs stone in Blackrose Prison, the stone in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the stone in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. A beast guards the Root; Cuts-the-Old-Knot brews a draught from drained sap strong enough to kill it, so she can reach the Eye. The orders aim: take the stones first, open the gate, use the Eye in place to heal the trees, bring the stones back to her so the chamber is sealed for good, and end the Unbound. She looks at the stones the player carries and names the places of those still missing.

record.title: No Name on the Work Roll
record.premise: A stranger sent up the river on an Owing barge gives the gang's cook their name and trade in the barge's hold, and is freed on the landing by a sour gang-master on an order from Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 1 (passed by the owner, 2026-11-17) and §1. The game opens in the hold of the Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing; the hold's door is locked. Okeeh, the gang's cook, asks the player's name (the "player's name set from a conversation" block: the stage after her line opens the game's own name entry) and their trade (a profession as in Morrowind: each answer sets a stage that raises five skills by five; one answer lets the player name their own five, one at a time, each pick a stage that raises that skill by five). When the trade is given the door is unlocked from outside. Dralin Uveran, the gang-master, speaks first on the landing (the quest's one speaks-first line), says the player's name was struck from his roll this morning on Vosh-Leera's order, and sends them to her house in Jal-Veesa, passing on the tree-minder's request for Sithis' beard from Reed-Sill Weir on the way. The player's pack holds two lockpicks. MN02 starts on this quest's stage 90 and carries the markers on the weir's moss and on Vosh-Leera's door. The side quest What the Herald Sent is left out: the main quest only. Okeeh and Dralin first answer the line's shared topics Hist, Jal-Veesa and the Owing.

The player's name was struck from the gang-master's roll this morning, on an order brought by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa: they owe no months and are free.

Jal-Veesa's tree-minder wants Sithis' beard, a grey moss hanging over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, which is on the road to the town.
A Hist is a great thinking tree, the size of a tower, with pale grey bark, roots standing out of the water and a pool of eggs at its foot; every Argonian village is built round one.

topics.label: Where am I?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: "You're in the hold of the work barge, moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel. This is Black Marsh, the Argonians' country." The barge brought this gang up from the sea to serve the Owing: months of owed work given by the marsh in place of a cell, served here cutting reed for the mat-makers of Stormhold. She is Okeeh, the gang's cook. The door is locked from outside, as it is for every new gang, until the gang-master, a Dunmer named Dralin Uveran, takes their names onto his roll; it will not be long. She does not know the player's face, and asks their name (a question; its answer is topic.mn01-name). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: My name? I'll tell you.
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: she listens and says the name back, so she can shout it at mealtimes. Does: sets stage 20, whose start opens the game's name entry; then she asks what the player did before the marsh caught them: "Every gang has a fighter, a hunter, a thief and someone who knows a poultice. What were you?" (a question; its answers are the seven trade topics). Checks: nothing.

topics.intent: Okeeh. topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Okeeh (and, by his own row, Dralin from stage 90). Tells: the Owing is the marsh's sentence. Black Marsh's own towns keep no jails; a debtor, a thief or a stranger who broke the peace is given months of owed work instead, and a broker sells those months to a gang-master like Dralin, who feeds the gang and works them until the months are served. Most of this gang owe six months or a year. Nobody counts a stranger's months kindly. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Owing?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: months of work owed instead of a cell; he buys them from the broker at Stormhold and his cutters work them off on the reed beds. The player's months were bought and are gone now, and that is his loss, not theirs. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Okeeh, an Argonian. Tells: a Hist is one of the great trees of Black Marsh, and they think. A Hist is as tall as a tower, with pale grey bark and roots standing up out of the water, and a pool at its foot where the eggs lie among the roots. Every Argonian village is built round its own tree. On a hatchling's naming day it licks its tree's sap, and the sap shapes it for life; her own tree is far to the south, and she still dreams of it. All the trees are joined at the root, so what one knows the others can know. An Argonian with a hand on the bark can hear them. They are not just trees: if a village's tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Dralin, a Dunmer. Tells: the Argonians' great trees, grey-barked and as big as towers, with an egg-pool at the foot; every village stands round one, and they say the trees think. He has seen men stand with a hand on one for an hour. Jal-Veesa's is the tall grey tree in the pool at the middle of the town, and it has looked poorly since the rains. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the town of the Veesa-Teeleel, the Sedge-Wardens, east up the road: stilt houses on mud banks round a pool, boat-lanes cut through the sedge, mats and fish drying on racks. The tall grey tree standing in the pool at the middle of the town is its Hist. She buys the gang's dried fish there. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Jal-Veesa?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the Sedge-Wardens' town, east up the road past Reed-Sill Weir: stilt houses round a pool with their Hist in the middle. Its elders answer to nobody in Stormhold, and its root-herald, Vosh-Leera, speaks for them to outsiders. Her house is in the town; any warden will point to it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: the gang's cook; she owes no months, she is paid, and she has cooked for Dralin's gangs four seasons. She sells dried fish and lamp oil from her stall by the hut. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Hara-Jeel. Tells: a reed-cutter of this gang, owing a year for a debt at Stormhold; he came up on the barge beside the player and does not know them either. The door opens when the gang-master wants it to. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (speaks first) You. Off the barge.
topics.intent: Dralin Uveran, a step from the hold's door as the player comes out. Tells: he is Dralin Uveran, gang-master here. The player's name is not on his roll: it was struck this morning, before they cut a single reed, on an order brought down the road by Vosh-Leera, the root-herald of Jal-Veesa, the one who speaks for that town's elders and its tree to outsiders. He cannot refuse a root-herald. "You must have friends in high places." He paid for the player's months and has lost them. She wants the player at her house in Jal-Veesa, east up the road; he does not know why and does not care to. While they are going that way: the town's tree-minder has asked every gang on the river for Sithis' beard, a grey moss that hangs over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, the weir-wardens' camp where the road meets the creek. Mind the crocodiles under the weir. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: the gang-master of Ashgate Landing, a Dunmer of Stormhold who buys Owing months and works them off on the reed. He has nothing more for the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who is Vosh-Leera?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: Jal-Veesa's root-herald. A root-herald speaks for a town's elders and its tree to anyone from outside, so an order from her is the town's order. She walked down this morning, gave the order and went back. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is Sithis' beard?
topics.intent: Dralin. Tells: a long grey moss that hangs from the trees over the creek below Reed-Sill Weir, the first camp on the road east. Tree-minders use it for something; Jal-Veesa's minder wants it badly. There are crocodiles under the weir where the wardens throw their offal; kill them, shoot them from the log walk on top of the weir, or keep out of their sight. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

The player picks Sithis' beard below Reed-Sill Weir, past or through two young crocodiles (fight, shoot from the log walk, or sneak), and brings it to Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, at the Hist pool. She shows the sick tree (dry dark bark, a closed scar, a cooling egg-pool), makes a poultice that warms the pool but does not open the scar, says what the town loses if the tree dies, and has the player lay a hand on the bark for the tree's blessing (the town's own shrine-blessing: waterbreathing, or resist poison for an Argonian). Vosh-Leera then tells the player who they now work for, how the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad tree to call Umbriel down, and why a stranger with no kin was chosen; she pays 50 gold and asks the player back to her house for a second task, which starts MN03. The jal-veesa-minder of the line is named Weeltul here.

truth.what: Jal-Veesa's Hist fell sick. Its bark dried and darkened, its scar closed and gives no sap, and its egg-pool has cooled. Weeltul cannot find a cause. Sithis' beard, laid in the pool as a poultice, warms the water for a while.

Vosh-Leera, root-herald of the town, began to pass what she heard to a Toh-Reel-Ka handler, without asking what was done with it. This season the order told her to find a stranger with no kin in the work gangs and free them, since such a stranger makes a cheap and useful spy; she chose the player from the barge's list.

The An-Xileel, who then ruled Black Marsh, used Lilmoth's mad Hist to call the flying city Umbriel down on the marsh; its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The An-Xileel fell. The Xeech-Leel rose by being their opposite, and in 4E 98 to 100 made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree and nobody allied with a tree could do it again.

topics.intent: Vosh-Leera, if the player comes before the moss is given. Tells: she did; she is Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. topics.label: What is a Hist?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: the great thinking tree every Argonian town stands round; this one is the tall grey tree in the pool behind her, Jal-Veesa's own. Its bark should be pale and soft; feel how dry it is now. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: she is Weeltul, tree-minder of Jal-Veesa: she tends the town's Hist, keeps its egg-pool and draws its sap; every hatchling of the town comes to her on its naming day. She is waiting on Sithis' beard from the weir. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I brought Sithis' beard from the weir.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Checks: hasItem [thing.mn02.sithis-beard, 1]. Tells: she takes it and lays it in the pool as a poultice. She shows the player the tree: its bark should be pale grey and soft and is dry and dark; its scar, the one place in the bark where she draws a little sap, has closed and gives nothing; its egg-pool, where the town's eggs lie among the roots, is cooling. The moss warms the water for a few days but does not open the scar. She does not know the cause; no minder on the river does. If the tree dies, no egg in its pools will ever hatch again, and in a generation Jal-Veesa is empty. She asks the player to lay a hand on the bark at the pool's edge: a tree gives its blessing to those its people trust, and the player brought the moss (the town's shrine-blessing: waterbreathing for a time, or, for an Argonian, who already breathes water, resist poison). Vosh-Leera is waiting in her house on the bank. Does: sets stage 30, whose start takes the moss.

topics.label: Tell me about the eggs.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: Argonian eggs are laid in the pool among a Hist's roots, and the tree keeps them warm and alive through its roots. If a tree's bond with its eggs is cut, the unborn die in the shell. A village whose tree dies has no future: nothing in its pools will hatch again. This pool is cooling; she has turned the eggs twice today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the sap?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: sap is what a Hist bleeds, amber-coloured and thick. A hatchling licks its tree's sap on its naming day, and the sap shapes its body for life. Drunk, it brings visions the tree sends, of far places; minders drink a little to ask the trees a question. It makes a fighter stronger for a time, which is why some steal it. In the old days the trees made it hard as stone, amber, but no tree does that now. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the scar?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: every Hist has one place in its bark, low on the trunk, where its minder cuts a little and the tree gives sap there and nowhere else; that is the scar. A healthy tree's scar weeps sap when it is opened. A sick tree's scar closes over and gives nothing. Jal-Veesa's closed this season. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells, in a line or two: a flying city that came down on Lilmoth long ago, called by the An-Xileel through Lilmoth's mad tree; every minder is taught it as a warning of what a tree can be made to do. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: root-herald of Jal-Veesa: she speaks for the town's elders and its tree to anyone from outside, Dunmer buyers and Stormhold's halls and gang-masters among them. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Why did you have me freed?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera, in her house, privately: nobody names the order aloud in company. Tells: the player has seen the tree. Trees are falling sick, one at a time, along the river, and nobody knows why. The people she answers to want it found. They are the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors: the elite order of the Xeech-Leel, the People of the New Beginning, who have ruled the province since the An-Xileel fell. In 4E 48 the An-Xileel, who ruled then, used the mad Hist of Lilmoth to call down the flying city Umbriel, and its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The Xeech-Leel made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree, and nobody allied with a tree, can ever turn on the marsh like that again. They comb the work gangs for strangers with no kin and no ties, because such a stranger makes a useful spy and a cheap one; she chose the player off the barge's list. Nobody in the marsh is owed a reason. They pay, and they give work. She gives the player fifty gold and asks them to come back to her, here, for a second task. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about the Toh-Reel-Ka.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Toh-Reel-Ka is Jel for "Secret Warriors": toh, secret, as in xal-toh, sacred secret, and reel-ka, warrior. They are the Xeech-Leel's order of spies and guards, made in the Void Nights, when the moons vanished and the province feared its trees were turning again. They watch the trees and anyone who seeks a tree's power, and they answer only to the Xeech-Leel's council at Helstrom. They wear no mark; their handlers keep quiet houses in the cities; people like her pass on what they hear. She has never asked what they do with it. Nobody names them aloud in company, and neither should the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Xeech-Leel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Xeech-Leel means the People of the New Beginning: Xeech, the planting month, and leel, people. They took the province in the generations after Umbriel by being everything the An-Xileel were not. Their first promise is that no faction may speak alone with a tree; they swore to govern in the open, and their council sits at Helstrom. They hold the old forts, roads and tolls through their Archwardens; inland the towns and tribes run themselves, as Jal-Veesa does. People call them "the Wardens", or "the New Beginning". Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: in 4E 48 the An-Xileel, who ruled Black Marsh then, sang to Lilmoth's Hist in secret until it went mad, and through it called down Umbriel, a flying city, onto the marsh. The city's dead killed the people of Lilmoth. The An-Xileel fell for it and their name went with them. That is why the province fears a tree turned to a faction's use, and why the order exists. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 3. Vosh-Leera gives the player a cup of sap (Skyrim's potion bottle under our name); the player drinks it in front of her by a line. The stage it sets fades the screen to black and shows the vision's words on a message box while it is black (the approved fade-with-message block); the player then tells it to her line by line, and she names Teel-Fen Weir, south of the town, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots. Heem-Jasa shows the grey paste in the young tree's closed scar and points to the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, where three Unbound sap-takers keep jars of sap. The player fights them, shoots them from cover or passes them by stealth to take the note (taking it moves the quest; a jar lies beside it to take as well). Back on the platform Heem-Jasa asks whether her tree will live: the truth opens her Alchemy training (Adept) and her stall; a comfort gives three potions of Cure Poison on the spot and leaves her training and stall closed. The note orders the crew to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, which starts MN04.

To prove me, she wants a jar of stolen sap from Keel-Raa, an Unbound go-between lodging at the Boatmen's Lodge with two hired men. I can lift it from his pack, buy it for a hundred gold, or fight the three of them for it, which the levy will not count as a crime. I'm to bring her the jar.

topics.label: Vosh-Leera sent me. The Unbound are draining the trees.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: she knows; she hears the player out: the sealed scar, the hide, the camp, Sesk's names. "The Eye" is the Eye of Argonia, the lost jewel of the old priest-kings, who ruled the marsh before any history was written; they cut it from Hist amber, the solid sap the trees no longer make. It lies at the Root, the place under the sea where the roots of every Hist meet, behind a gate that the last king sealed, in a place no living diver has found. Cuts-the-Old-Knot wants it. She asks what the player thinks the draught is for (a question; its answer is topic.mn05-draught). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Sap makes a fighter strong. Something must guard the Root, and she means to kill it.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: (after topic.mn05-report: the Eye of Argonia is the priest-kings' jewel of Hist amber, at the Root under the sea behind a sealed gate) she agrees: whatever guards the Root, Cuts-the-Old-Knot means to kill it. Now she wants proof of the player. Keel-Raa, an Unbound go-between, lodges at the Boatmen's Lodge, the inn by the city landing, with two hired men and a jar of stolen sap in his pack. Bring her the jar. He is not looking for a fight and will talk, so lift it from his pack, buy it, or take it by force: his band pays the levy to look away from them, so the levy will not count it a crime either. Does: sets stage 20. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about the Eye of Argonia.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: the priest-kings cut it from Hist amber in the oldest days, when the trees still made sap hard as stone. It is said to be the knot that joins every root to every other; used where it sits, it can pour strength down every root. Relic-hunters have chased it for centuries; most chase glass. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Root?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: every Hist is joined to every other at the root. Under the sea, somewhere off the coast, the roots of every tree meet in one place: the Root. The priest-kings built over it, and the last of them sealed its gate. Nobody living knows the way down. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me the order's history.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: Toh-Reel-Ka is Jel for Secret Warriors. The Xeech-Leel made the order in the Void Nights, 4E 98 to 100, when the moons vanished and the province feared its trees were turning again, as the sworn guard of the Root Talk, the great gathering of the tribes at Helstrom, and of Lilmoth's third tree. Its one charge has not changed: no tree, and no person or group allied with a tree, may bring another Umbriel. It answers to the council of the Xeech-Leel and to nobody else. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

Tells: lowest first, Voh-Vastei, "Apprentice"; Toh-Wo, "Secret-Speaker", one who brings secrets in; Reel-Ka, "Warrior", a full member; Ka-Deelith, "War-Teacher", who trains the warriors; and Toh-Nassa, "Leader of the Secret". Each rank brings gear and gold, and the order's doors open wider. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 6, as passed by the owner. Kept: the glass Eye in Gideon's market, the dealer who admits it for a few coins or a little Speech, the smugglers of the South Watch who kept the old silver setting in a locked chest in the ruin's inner room (Old Laboratory's one interior), the Collector's courteous note in the chest, the ship's name scratched inside the setting and Nesh-Deeka's reading of it. Filled from the plot and the lore, smallest reading first: the dealer's name (Ovinius Calo, a Nibenese-descended trader of Gideon); a third way to the dealer's fact (his note from the South Watch, carried, to pickpocket or take from his body); the lock's level (Apprentice) and the key on the smugglers' boss; the Unbound's visit to Gideon's market that Nesh-Deeka already knows of.

truth.what: The Pale Harvest, a Company freighter, sank with a Gideon dealer's whole stock aboard; an old silver setting with no stone, its ship's name scratched inside, was among it.
Salvagers sold the setting to the smugglers; the smugglers put a garnet of green-red glass in it and sold the glass alone to Ovinius Calo as the Eye of Argonia, keeping the silver to melt.
Two Unbound asked after the Eye at Ovinius's stall and went away when they saw it was glass.
The Collector, Ennodius Vanin, slipped into the inner room, opened the chest, found the setting of no use to him and left a note for whoever came next.

record.title: The Grey Tooth
record.premise: The Toh-Reel-Ka's new Toh-Wo follows the parchment map to the Grey Tooth on Skeith Isle, gets past the Collector's men to learn the kings' stone was carried off to the Stormwidow, takes it from under the Unbound scouts in the beached wreck's hold, hears a wounded scout's word about the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth, and brings the stone to Never-Writes-Twice.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (story/design/quests/lines/main-plot.md §5 quest 11, passed by the owner), and invents nothing it does not give beyond the names listed in the review (L8). The quest starts on MN10's last stage (90, its completed ending): Never-Writes-Twice, now the player's officer at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom, has read the parchment map and marked the Grey Tooth. It uses the crag's small cave on the north face and the Stormwidow's sand-filled hold only; the cairn, its cache and the stern's strongbox belong to Bramman's Brethren and are never named as targets. The Collector's three hired men at the foot of the goat-path and in the cave, and the three Unbound scouts and the wounded scout at the wreck, are switched on by stage 10's start (the player is in Helstrom, another cell far away), so a player of the Brethren's line who comes first meets neither. Each step is a thing read or taken or a line picked: reading the Collector's rubbing moves the player on to the wreck; taking the marker stone moves them to the wounded scout; her words (or, if she is dead, the scrap of bark she carried) move them to the report; Never-Writes-Twice's report line completes the quest, which starts MN12 (the player's own errand to the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth) and MN13 (the hunt: Bell Station) together. The seal's recipe is optional: reading it teaches the poison's ingredients, and three bottles of the poison lie with it. Who the quest cannot go on without: Never-Writes-Twice.

truth.what: The captain of the Stormwidow, a ship of Bramman's Brethren, found a carved stone of the old kings in a niche of the cave and had it carried aboard. His men scratched on the niche's lintel in Cyrodilic that the stone went to the Stormwidow by her captain's order. Weeks later the Archwardens' privateers ran the ship onto Skeith Isle's south-west beach and killed her crew (the wreck's place history).

The Collector, who hunts the Eye, sent hired men to dig the cave. They found the empty niche. Vanin took a rubbing of the lintel's scratch, wrote his own lines under it and left it in the cave for his men, then sold the wreck's name to the Unbound for gold (plot §4, the Collector tells what he learns to whoever pays). His men still dig in case the stone came back.

Unbound scouts camped in the sand-filled hold and search its ballast crates for the stone. They carry their leader's recipe for the seal and three bottles of it. Tah-Leesh, one of them, fell through a rotten deck onto the beach below the bow, and the others left her there, unable to walk.

Tah-Leesh has heard Cuts-the-Old-Knot say that whoever serves the Toh-Reel-Ka should ask what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth. She does not know the answer. She scratched the words on a scrap of bark to keep them.

Never-Writes-Twice reads the marker stone's seven towers as the drowned spires off Lilmoth and sends the player to the divers of Bell Station. Asked about Fort Chalkmoth, she says it is a fort like any other. She lies (plot §3).

record.title: The Cellar Door
record.premise: On their own account, the Toh-Wo gets into Fort Chalkmoth's keep by the wall captain's price or by the trapdoor in the yard, finds jars of Jal-Veesa's sap stacked by the stair in the quartermaster's store, faces the order's gaoler in the guardroom, and finds the cellar's inner door locked with moaning behind it and its key not in the fort.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (§5 quest 12, passed by the owner). The player's own errand, begun by the wounded scout's words and Never-Writes-Twice's answer in MN11; it runs beside MN13 (the hunt) and either may come first. Four steps in the plot's order where it gives one: the way in (the captain's price, or the trapdoor in the yard unseen), then the store, the gaoler and the door, which the player may do in any order once inside, as one working stage (quest-write §3.4) with three objectives. The fort's main source, Fort Neugrad, gives the keep (its Adept lock serves as the store's door) and the prison below it (the cellar), whose passage door is set as the trapdoor in the yard and comes up into the guardroom. The gaoler's test is the "spell cast in front of a person as a test" block (owner, #73), to be proven once; until proven the gate stands in as Illusion 25. The plot has two people speak first (the wall captain at the gate and the gaoler); the ceiling allows one, so the gaoler speaks first (every way in meets him) and the captain stands at the gate with a marker and the objective. The cellar's question stays open: the player learns only that sap from Jal-Veesa is stored by the stair in a fort with no Hist, the gaoler's "they sleep, and they dream", and moaning behind a door whose key is not in the fort. The last stage turns the player back to the hunt: to Bell Station if MN13 is not yet done, to the seal-stones if it is.

record.premise: Bell Station's steward names Teku-Sul as the marked tower; the Toh-Wo makes the long dive, gets past the drowned priests' attendants to a great gate with three empty sockets, hears from a priest's ghost what the three seal-stones are and where each went, and is made a Reel-Ka by Never-Writes-Twice, who sends them after all three.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (§5 quest 13, passed by the owner). The hunt, begun by MN11's report beside the player's own errand to Fort Chalkmoth (MN12); either may come first. topics.label: (speaks first)
topics.intent: Corvus Ulvius, outside the gate. Tells: this is the Rose, and the Blackguards' heirs born in it hold it now; strangers who walk in are killed on the walls. He lets a stranger in as a guest three ways: 300 gold to him, words good enough to move him, or a duel with him, fists and steel, until one yields. A guest walks the yard and the hall and nobody touches them. Anyone who climbs the walls without his leave is fair game, and anyone who kills him has the whole Rose to fight. If the player asks what they want inside, he says the raj-kaal Okaz-Teel keeps the old warden's vault in his hall and the key on his belt, and he already has a buyer for what lies in it, the Imperial in the hall. Offers topic.mn14-toll, topic.mn14-persuade and topic.mn14-duel as answers. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Here is your toll. (300 gold)
topics.intent: Corvus. Checks: goldAtLeast 300. Tells: he waves the player in as a guest of the Rose; the walls will let them be. Does: takes 300 gold; sets stage 20. Fallback: no coin, no gate; words or steel are the other ways.

topics.label: (Persuade) The Toh-Reel-Ka can send you a hundred like me. Let one in quietly instead.
topics.intent: Corvus. Checks: skillAtLeast [Speech, 75]. Tells: he laughs and lets the player in as a guest, since a quiet Reel-Ka is cheaper than a loud one. Does: sets stage 20. Fallback: words are wind at this gate; the player is left the toll or a duel, and this line is not offered again.

topics.label: I'll fight you for the gate.
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: he likes that; until one of them yields; if he yields, the player walks in as a guest; if the player kills him, the Rose fights them. Does: sets stage 15 (the duel begins, the yield block).

topics.label: (on yielding)
topics.intent: Corvus, when he yields. Tells: enough; he gives the gate; the player is a guest of the Rose and nobody on the walls will touch them. Does: sets flag.mn14.yielded (stage 20).

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: captain of the Rose's gate, born in its cells like his father and his father's mother; he keeps the gate because he has not lost a fight at it in eleven years.

topics.label: Who are the Blackguards' heirs?
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the Rose was the Empire's prison, built for Argonians; when the Empire left, the prisoners' children took it for their own and call it the Rose; they live by the road and the boat, and they answer to the raj-kaal, Okaz-Teel, a Naga of the deep swamp.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Okaz-Teel, in his hall (talks only to a guest; at 25 a player who speaks to him is seen). Tells: he is the raj-kaal of the Rose, the war-chief of its people; a Naga is an Argonian of the deep swamp, and he says it with pride. The warden's vault in his wall holds a thief's old stone; the Imperial has offered for it and been told to wait; the key is on his belt and goes to whoever pays 1,000 gold first. He watches his own belt, and his people watch the vault, and a thief they see is a thief they kill.

topics.label: I'll buy the key to the warden's vault. (1000 gold)
topics.intent: Okaz-Teel. Checks: goldAtLeast 1000. Tells: the Imperial waited too long; he gives the key and says the stone is the player's. Does: sets stage 22 (takes 1,000 gold, gives the key and the chest's contents). Fallback: 1,000 gold, not a coin less; the Imperial can still outbid a pauper.

topics.label: (greeting)
topics.intent: The Collector, in the hall (he never fights and never calls the guards). Tells: so the Toh-Reel-Ka's hound has found him again; he left the player a note in Gideon; he has offered for the stone and been told to wait, and he will not bid against the order. He has a side errand for a capable hand: a riddle, not a road, and the Eye can wait for it; what lies at the end of it is made for whatever guards the Root. (The side quest itself is its own record.)

topics.label: That ring on your finger. What is it?
topics.intent: The Collector. Tells: Kothringi silver, from a knight's barrow in the Kotherra; it steadies the hand at a lock or a pocket; it is not for sale. If the player asks what he would lose: alive he is worth more to them than the ring, for his errand; a dead man gives no riddles.

topics.label: The Collector
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the Imperial paid the toll like an honest man, which nobody here trusts; he sits in the hall as the raj-kaal's guest waiting to buy the stone.

topics.label: Umbriel
topics.intent: Corvus. Tells: the flying city came down on Lilmoth when his grandmother was a girl; its dead came as far as the Rose's walls and the walls held.

topics.label: Remind me what we are hunting, and why.
topics.intent: Never-Writes-Twice, at the back of Nesh-Deekas House. Tells: the Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings jewel, cut from Hist amber. It sits at the Root, the place under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire where the roots of every Hist meet. Used where it sits, it pours strength down every root and heals every sick tree; lifted from its place, it cuts every tree from every other for good. The last king shut it behind the Kings Gate, which opens only with its three seal-stones: the thiefs stone in Blackrose Prison, the stone in the flooded vaults of Gemin and the stone in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. A beast guards the Root; Cuts-the-Old-Knot brews a draught from drained sap strong enough to kill it, so she can reach the Eye. The orders aim: take the stones first, open the gate, use the Eye in place to heal the trees, bring the stones back to her so the chamber is sealed for good, and end the Unbound. She looks at the stones the player carries and names the places of those still missing.
